content: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) principles: Combine cultural, biological, and chemical control methods. Monitor pest populations regularly. Use pest thresholds to decide when to spray. Rotate chemical classes to prevent resistance. Encourage natural predators.

Soil health best practices: Test soil annually for pH, NPK, and micronutrients. Maintain organic matter above 2%. Use crop rotation to break disease cycles. Avoid soil compaction. Consider green manure crops between seasons.

Water management for disease prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation when possible. Water early in the morning so foliage dries quickly. Ensure proper drainage to prevent waterlogging. Drip irrigation reduces foliar disease pressure significantly.

Organic disease management: Neem oil (2ml/L) acts as broad-spectrum fungicide and insecticide. Trichoderma viride (2g/L) as soil drench for root diseases. Pseudomonas fluorescens (5g/L) foliar spray for bacterial diseases. Bordeaux mixture (1%) for fungal diseases.

Weather impact on crop diseases: High humidity (>80%) promotes fungal diseases. Rain splash spreads soil-borne pathogens. Warm temperatures (25-30C) accelerate disease development. Cool, wet conditions favor downy mildews and bacterial diseases.
